name: @ham2k/extension-sdk
description: Write extensions for the Ham2K Logger: typed hook contracts and the host API
author: Sebastian Delmont <sd@ham2k.com>
//exports: `./package.json` is exported because an `exports` map without it makes the
file unreadable through package resolution: Node refuses an undeclared
subpath, so a tool asking this package its own version is told the package
does not exist. Common enough that npm's own docs call it out.
//ham2k-source: A condition only this repo's own test run asks for (`--conditions=ham2k-source`),
so a test can import the SDK by name and get the TypeScript sources rather
than a build of them — the same thing esbuild's alias does when it bundles an
extension. Deliberately not the conventional `development`: the published
tarball ships `dist` and not `src`, and a consumer who happened to run with
that common condition would be pointed at files their install does not have.
//sideEffects: Importing any of these modules does nothing observable, so a bundler may
drop whichever ones an extension never reaches. dxcc is the exception and
is named rather than waved through: it registers the built-in country file
at import time, and a bundler that dropped it would leave callsign
//peerDependencies: The libraries the extension host carries. An extension does NOT need these
installed: the build preset rewrites each one the manifest declares into a
lookup on the host's single instance, before esbuild ever resolves it, and
the published .d.ts carries their types rolled in. They are here, optional,
for the one case that does reach the filesystem — `inline: [...]`, which
ships your own copy because you need a version the host does not carry.
